_comment: system-map settings. Copied to ~/.leanscale-gtm/system-map.json by the :setup skill. Edit it by hand any time — every key has a _<key>_help line beside it, and keys starting with an underscore are documentation and are ignored by the scripts. The shared org profile lives next to this file in ~/.leanscale-gtm/profile.json and is read by every LeanScale GTM agent.
_environment_help: production | sandbox | developer. Labels the report and stops you acting on a sandbox finding in production. Salesforce reports this as Organization.IsSandbox; HubSpot as accountType on /account-info/v3/details.
_org_label_help: How this instance is named in the report title. Use the same wording your team uses in conversation.
_include_managed_packages_help: Inventory installed managed packages and use their namespaces as the strongest tool-detection signal. Turn off only if you already track packages elsewhere.
_include_integration_users_help: Inventory service accounts, their last login and their write surface. This is the section security reviews ask for.
_include_connected_apps_help: Inventory connected apps and OAuth grants, and flag the orphaned ones. HubSpot has no public API for this — see hubspot_connected_apps in the run skill for the manual export.
_include_automation_help: Inventory flows, workflow rules, Apex triggers, validation rules and assignment rules. Turning this off also disables conflict detection, which is the most valuable output here.
_include_scheduled_jobs_help: Include scheduled jobs and scheduled flows. These carry a true last-fired timestamp, so they are the most reliable dormancy signal available.
_dormancy_days_help: An automation, app or integration user idle for this many days is reported as dormant. 90 catches a full quarter of seasonality; drop to 30 for a fast-moving instance, raise to 180 if you have annual processes.
_recent_change_days_help: Window for 'what changed recently'. Set it to match the period you would investigate when a number moves unexpectedly.
_flag_orphaned_automation_help: Flag active automation whose last editor no longer has an active account. Set false only if your platform deactivates leavers in a way that makes this noisy.
_believed_tools_help: The tools your team believes are connected to the CRM, captured during setup BEFORE anything was measured. The run compares this list against what the instance actually shows: tools detected but not listed are the finding, tools listed but not detected are the second finding. Replace this sample with your own answer — do not leave it as shipped.
_conflict_ignore_fields_help: Object.Field targets to exclude from conflict detection. Use for fields you have deliberately decided may be written by several systems. Keep it short — every entry here is a finding you have chosen not to see.
_ignore_automation_names_help: Automation names to exclude entirely, matched case-insensitively. Useful for vendor-managed automation you cannot change.
_ignore_namespaces_help: Managed-package namespace prefixes to leave out of the package inventory and the stack map.
_extra_integration_user_patterns_help: Extra substrings that identify a service account in your naming convention, e.g. 'robot', 'ops-bot', 'northwind-svc'. The built-in list already covers svc_, api_, integration, sync, connector, noreply and similar.
_object_surface_min_records_help: An object needs at least this many records before 'holds records but carries no automation' is worth reporting. Raise it if your instance has many small reference objects.
_allow_empty_automation_help: Leave false. When false, a run that finds zero automation across every surface aborts rather than producing a clean-looking empty report — because that result is almost always a permissions failure. Set true only after you have confirmed the instance genuinely has no automation.
